messages:
Alex M.: heads up — p99 ingest latency on collector-prod climbed from ~120ms to ~420ms around 06:30 UTC, downstream exporters started queueing. collector CPU jumped to ~95% on three nodes :thinking:
Priya S.: saw the alert, checking traces. did you already correlate by tenant?
Alex M.: quick grep: top 5 tenants account for ~78% of spans in the 06:20-06:40 window. looks like one heavy customer increased trace volume (long tail of single-request fanout).
Mateo R.: exporter backpressure symptoms? exporters returning 429s or grpc timeouts?
Alex M.: exporter errors were mostly "resource exhausted" / grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and occasional "stream closed" from the OTLP-gRPC exporter. queue length metric spiked.
Jamie (infra): pulling collector logs now. also noticing GC churn on the collector JVM pod (heap ~3.2G, old gen spikes).
Sam K.: what's the current span processor config? batch vs simple? flush_interval?
Alex M.: batch processor with these settings: ```batch_timeout_millis: 2000 max_export_batch_size: 512 schedule_delay_millis: 200``` (OTel collector.yaml snippet).
Priya S.: can you paste the exact collector config? thinking: if max_export_batch_size is large and exporter blocking, it can accumulate many spans in memory.
Alex M.: pasted above. also exporters have compression gzip enabled, but we saw slow downstream ack times from kafka-exporter consumer group.
Mateo R.: hypothesis: downstream exporter (kafka) became slow -> batch fills -> memory + CPU for batching + serialization -> increased p99 latency and GC -> more delays (feedback loop).
Jamie (infra): verified: kafka consumer lag jumped 3-4x in that period, and network egress for those pods was saturated on 10Gb link (burst).
Sam K.: what about sampling? are we sampling before exporting?
Alex M.: not at the collector level for that tenant; sampling is done upstream in app for some customers but not enforced. heavy tenant wasn't sampling.
Priya S.: short-term mitigations? reduce max_export_batch_size, lower batch_timeout, enable per-tenant tail-sampling or queue caps.
Mateo R.: I ran a local sim with same batch settings and a slow exporter; lowering max_export_batch_size to 128 and schedule_delay to 100ms reduced memory pressure dramatically and kept p99 closer to baseline.
Sam K.: can we apply a config change and rollout as canary to 10% of collector pods? measure p99 over 30m then roll further.
Jamie (infra): yes — we can create a new configmap and a partial rollout via label selector to a daemonset subset. I'll prepare a canary doc.
Alex M.: also proposing: per-tenant exporter routing so heavy tenants can go to dedicated pipeline (dedicated kafka topic or dedicated consumer group) to avoid noisy neighbor.
Priya S.: agree. mid-term: add adaptive sampling at collector with a light-weight reservoir sampler and per-tenant caps. also consider throttling spans per-second per-tenant.
Mateo R.: other optimizations: enable batched compression and smaller batches + keepalive tuning for OTLP gRPC, plus switch to protobuf batching instead of JSON (we already use protobuf, but double-check serializers).
Sam K.: note: changing batch_size affects throughput/cost tradeoff. smaller batches -> higher CPU/tokens for serialization and more ops downstream. need to measure unit cost.
Alex M.: good point. we'll track token/sec and CPU delta in the canary. also instrument the collector for exporter queue length and per-exporter latency histograms (p50/p95/p99).
Jamie (infra): rollout plan: 1) canary config (max_export_batch_size=128, schedule_delay_millis=100) to 10% collectors for 1h, 2) if stable, 50% for 3h, 3) full rollout with a migration doc. I'll open a PR with config and k8s rollout manifest.
Priya S.: fallback policy: if p99 increases or CPU > 80% on canaries, revert immediately. add alert for exporter queue length > 50k.
Mateo R.: I'll add a small script for local load testing to simulate heavy tenant (span open/close fanout) so we can benchmark before/after.
Alex M.: thanks — action owners: Jamie infra handles canary deploy; Mateo loadtests + perf report; Priya designs sampling/tenant caps; Sam to model cost impact. I'll follow up with summary and timeline. :thumbsup:
telemetry-bot: incident-note created: "collector-p99-spike-1772345600" — linked to runbook ID 42.
Priya S.: one more: consider gating retention/ingest path for top offenders (auto-notify product + sales) — if a customer increases fanout dramatically, we may need SLA changes.
Alex M.: agreed. adding product & billing in follow-up.
Sam K.: leaving a quick paste of the canary config snippet I'll use: ```processors:
  batch/canary:
    timeout: 100ms
    send_batch_max_size: 128
exporters:
  otlp/grpc:
    endpoint: kafka-exporter.svc:4317
    compression: gzip
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [batch/canary]
      exporters: [otlp/grpc]
```
Jamie (infra): PR opened: #3126 with canary config and manifest. linking to thread.
Alex M.: ok let's run the canary. update this thread with timings and metrics. thanks everyone.
